chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Jareer, from Sadeer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who goes to the animal, he said: He is penalized less than the (complete) Penalty (Hadd), and he must compensate the price of the animal to its owner, because he has spoiled it for him. It is slaughtered, burnt, and buried if it is from those whose flesh is eaten; and if it is from those whose back is ridden upon, he must compensate its price, be whipped less than the (complete) Penalty (Hadd), and it is taken out from the city in which the act was committed with it to other lands where it is not known, so that it is sold there, lest it be scoffed at with it.

key_terms.يُحَدُّ دُونَ الْحَدِّ: penalized less than the complete Hadd

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal penalty and procedure for bestiality according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific fiqh of *Jariyah* (lesser punishment) for bestiality, distinguishing it from the full *Hadd* by imposing financial compensation (*Gharamah*) to the owner and the destruction or relocation of the animal to preserve social dignity. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the act corrupts the animal's utility, necessitating its removal from public view to prevent the perpetrator from being stigmatized by the very creature he defiled.
